title: luscombeu/utrannotation pipeline parameters
description: Add CAGE-supported 5' UTRs (spliced-leader aware) and polyA-signal-refined 3' UTRs to EGAPx genome annotations

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file with one row per genome annotation.
input.help_text: A comma-separated file with a header row and one row per genome annotation, with the columns `id`, `genome` (FASTA), `annotation` (EGAPx GFF3), `tss` (a luscombeu/cagescan results directory, or a BED file of TSS clusters from any CAGE workflow) and, for BED input, an optional `tss_sl` (BED of spliced-leader acceptor clusters). See the usage docs.

cluster_set.description: cagescan TSS cluster set to use (cagescan input only): `broad` (CAGEfightR or paraclu) or `sharp` (RECLU, reproducible across replicates).

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

utr5_options.title: 5' UTR options
utr5_options.description: Choice of the CAGE TSS that becomes the 5' end of each transcript (5' UTR of coding mRNAs).

tss_max_dist.description: Maximum 5' UTR length of coding mRNAs, and maximum 5' end move of non-coding transcripts, in bases along the transcript.

tss_selection.description: Which qualifying TSS to use. `auto`: the strongest mature-mRNA 5' end (SL acceptors, and non-SL TSSs downstream of every qualifying acceptor); `closest_atg`: the shortest 5' UTR; `dominant`: the highest count.
tss_selection.help_text: `auto` suits metazoans with or without trans-splicing: without SL data it is the dominant TSS (the CAGE convention); with SL data a non-SL peak upstream of an SL acceptor, which may be the start of the outron (short-lived pre-mRNA), cannot win. See docs/rationale.md.

tss_min_rel.description: Minimum TSS count relative to the strongest reference TSS (by default the whole EGAPx 5' UTR; see `--tss_rel_whole_utr`), to ignore weak exonic CAGE peaks.

tss_rel_whole_utr.description: Compare `--tss_min_rel` with the strongest TSS anywhere in the EGAPx 5' UTR (also beyond `--tss_max_dist`), not only within the window.
tss_rel_whole_utr.help_text: With the default, a weak peak near the ATG cannot trim a 5' UTR whose strong TSS lies further away than `--tss_max_dist`; such mRNAs keep the EGAPx 5' end. Set to false to compare only with the peaks within `--tss_max_dist`.

tss_min_count.description: Minimum pooled CAGE count of a TSS (summed over samples).

utr5_min_len.description: Minimum 5' UTR length of a TSS. 0 accepts a TSS at the ATG, as at spliced-leader acceptors next to the start codon.

sl_min_fraction.description: Minimum fraction of spliced-leader READ1s for a TSS to be labelled `sl` instead of `nosl`.

tss_noncoding.description: Also move the 5' end of lncRNAs and other non-coding transcripts (EGAPx misc_RNA) to the strongest CAGE TSS within `--tss_max_dist` of their EGAPx 5' end.

sl_window_up.description: SL acceptor rule: non-SL TSSs up to this many bases upstream of a qualifying SL acceptor are ignored when choosing a transcript's TSS and when splitting operons (-1: no limit).
sl_window_up.help_text: Within a few bases of an acceptor, non-SL peaks are SL reads without a recognisable leader (e.g. reads that keep only the leader's final AG map to the A of the acceptor AG, 2 nt upstream). Further away, tunicates have genuine non-trans-spliced TSSs a few tens of nt upstream (Ciona; Matsumoto et al. 2010) or downstream (O. dioica testis; Danks et al. 2018) of acceptors, so the default window is kept small. See docs/rationale.md.

sl_window_down.description: SL acceptor rule: non-SL TSSs up to this many bases downstream of a qualifying SL acceptor (inside the mature mRNA) are ignored when choosing a transcript's TSS and when splitting operons (-1: the whole 5' UTR).
sl_window_down.help_text: Within a few bases of an acceptor, non-SL peaks are SL reads without a recognisable leader (e.g. reads that keep only the leader's final AG map to the A of the acceptor AG, 2 nt upstream). Further away, tunicates have genuine non-trans-spliced TSSs a few tens of nt upstream (Ciona; Matsumoto et al. 2010) or downstream (O. dioica testis; Danks et al. 2018) of acceptors, so the default window is kept small. See docs/rationale.md.

utr3_options.title: 3' UTR options
utr3_options.description: Evidence used to set the 3' end of each coding mRNA.

keep_polya_evidence.description: Keep the EGAPx 3' end of models supported by poly(A)-tail reads (`experiment=COORDINATES: polyA evidence`).

pas_motifs.description: Comma-separated polyadenylation-signal motifs (DNA, RNA sense). AATAAA and ATTAAA are the two most common signals at human polyA sites (~53-58% and ~15-17%; Tian & Graber 2012).

pas_window.description: Maximum distance of the polyadenylation signal from the EGAPx 3' end, in bases along the transcript.

pas_offset.description: Bases from the motif end to the new 3' end. The signal lies within ~40 nt upstream of the cleavage site (Tian & Graber 2012); 15 is a typical spacing.

operon_options.title: Trans-splicing and operon options
operon_options.description: Spliced-leader (SL) labels and operons. Operons need SL data: they are annotated only for genomes whose cagescan results have SL counts, and only with --trans_splicing.

trans_splicing.description: Use the spliced-leader counts of the cagescan results, or the `tss_sl` BED, to label TSSs `sl` / `nosl`. Genomes without SL data are all `nosl` either way.
trans_splicing.help_text: Set to false to ignore SL data: every TSS is `nosl`, no `trans_splice_acceptor_site` rows are written and no operons are annotated.

operons.description: Annotate operons for genomes with SL data. Set to false for trans-splicing organisms without operons.
operons.help_text: Eukaryotic operons depend on SL trans-splicing, but trans-splicing does not imply operons: in many trans-splicing animals most SL genes are monocistronic. Operons are never annotated for genomes without SL counts.

operon_gap_from.description: How intergenic distances are measured: `cds` (stop codon to start codon), `transcript` (transcript ends) or `evidence` (transcript ends when the upstream 3' end is supported by PAS or poly(A) reads and the downstream 5' end by CAGE, otherwise CDS).
operon_gap_from.help_text: Transcript-end distances would be the true intercistronic regions, but annotated UTR ends are imprecise; on I69 EGAPx and O10 they gave less SL-consistent operons than `cds`.

operon_max_gap.description: Same-strand genes whose stop-to-start codon distance is below this join an operon (CDS distances; also the fallback of `--operon_gap_from evidence`).
operon_max_gap.help_text: 500 is Plessy et al. 2024's definition (gene models without UTRs). On the I69 EGAPx and O10 annotations, CDS windows of 400-500 gave the most SL-consistent operons, and the Ganot et al. 2004 cyclin D3 operon needs at least 404 (its largest CDS gap is 403); see docs/rationale.md.

operon_max_gap_tx.description: With `--operon_gap_from transcript` or `evidence`: distances between transcript ends below this join genes.
operon_max_gap_tx.help_text: On I69 EGAPx, 96-97% of CAGE-supported downstream genes 0-60 nt from the previous transcript start at an SL acceptor, 86% at 61-100 nt and 65% at 101-200 nt; O. dioica intercistronic regions are 23-30 nt (Ganot et al. 2004) and C. elegans operon genes are ~100 bp apart (Blumenthal et al. 2015).

operon_split_min_count.description: Minimum pooled count of a non-SL TSS that splits an operon, and of an SL TSS that shields a non-SL TSS next to it.

operon_split_rule.description: When a non-SL TSS between two genes splits an operon. `dominant`: only if it is stronger than every SL TSS between the genes; `any`: at any non-SL TSS; `none`: distance only.
operon_split_rule.help_text: On C. elegans, splits at a non-SL TSS weaker than an SL TSS in the same gap were wrong (the pair is a WormBase operon pair) 65% of the time, against 9% when the non-SL TSS dominated; `dominant` raised adjacent-pair precision/recall from 0.432/0.478 to 0.443/0.516. When the SL data contain no SL TSS (leader not detected), AG-preceded TSSs are taken as SL acceptors. See docs/rationale.md.

operon_biotypes.description: Comma-separated gene_biotype values of the genes grouped into operons, or `all`.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
